contentBlocks.text: Sol is a curious puppet today — Sol wants to know everyone's name! Sol will go around the circle asking a big question.
Listen for Sol's question: [[¿cómo te llamas?]] — that means 'what is your name?' When Sol asks you, answer 'Me llamo... (your name)!'
Sol uses the word [[tú]] to mean 'you' when talking to a friend — just like yo means 'I' when talking about yourself. Ask a friend or family member: '¿Cómo te llamas tú?'
You asked and answered ¿cómo te llamas? using tú and yo — a real conversation! Tomorrow, you'll help Sol sort niños and niñas.

config.instructions: Match the Spanish word to its meaning.

objectives: Recognize and respond to the question ¿cómo te llamas? (what is your name?) with me llamo... (my name is...)
Use tú (you) when asking a friend or family member their name
materialsNeeded: A few family members or stuffed animals to complete an 'interview' circle (works fine with just you and your child too)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Have Sol turn to your child and ask, in a curious voice, '¿Cómo te llamas?'
2. Coach your child to answer 'Me llamo... (their name)!' — echo it together a few times until it feels natural.
3. Explain simply that tú means 'you' when we talk to a friend, the same way yo means 'I' when we talk about ourselves.
4. Have your child become the interviewer: ask Sol, then a stuffed animal, then a family member, '¿Cómo te llamas tú?' and listen for the answer.
5. Go around the room 'interviewing' 3-4 more 'guests', switching who asks and who answers.
6. Complete the on-screen matching activity together, reading each tile aloud since your child may not read yet.
7. Close by asking: 'What does Sol ask when Sol wants to know your name? What do you say back?'
differentiationTips: Struggling: skip tú for today and focus only on hearing ¿cómo te llamas? and answering me llamo... — tú can be added once the question-and-answer pattern feels automatic
Ready for more: have your child interview every family member and a pet, keeping track of how many 'names' they collected
The question is long for a first echo — it's fine if your child only catches 'te llamas' at first and grows into the full question over the week
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a spoken question-and-answer activity — success looks like your child recognizing ¿cómo te llamas? and attempting 'me llamo... (their name)' in response, not a written answer. In the matching game: me llamo → 🙋, ¿cómo te llamas? → ❓, yo → 😀, tú → 👉.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Continues week 2's WA-WL-2015.1.1 target by turning yesterday's one-way name-sharing into a real two-way exchange — asking and answering — which is the heart of ACTFL Interpersonal Communication, and recycles yo alongside its counterpart tú in the matching activity.
